chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:
Whoever steals secretly by snatching it away, his hand is not cut off, but he is to be beaten severely.

key_terms.ضَرْبًا شَدِيدًا: a severe beating; a strong discretionary punishment
key_terms.لَمْ يُقْطَعْ: the hand is not cut off; the hadd of amputation is not applied
key_terms.يُضْرَبُ: he is beaten; corporal punishment is administered

ai.seo_question: Does secret snatching or stealthy taking require amputation in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling distinguishing stealthy snatching from theft that entails the hadd punishment of amputation. It states that in such a case, the hadd is not applied, but a severe discretionary beating is imposed instead.
